02Stress

Slide 10

Force of resistance per unit area offered by a body against deformation

  • Where,
  • σ - Stress in ‘Pascal (or) N/m2’
  • P - External force or load in ‘N’
  • A - Cross section area in ‘m2’

03Strain

Slide 11

Ratio of Change in dimension to original dimension of an object under application of external force is strain

  • Where,
  • ε - Strain (no unit)
  • dL - Change in dimension in ‘m’
  • L - Original dimension in ‘m’

04Types of stress

Slide 12

Only two basic stresses exists :

Normal stress (σ)

Shear stress (τ)

Other stresses either are similar to these basic stresses or are a combination of these e.g. bending stress is a combination of tensile, compressive and shear stresses. Torsional stress, as encountered in twisting of a shaft is a shearing stress.

Slide 13

Normal stresses/Linear stress/ Direct stress (σ): If the stresses are normal to the areas concerned, then these are termed as normal stresses.

Slide 14

Shear stresses (τ) : Where the cross sectional area of a block of material is subject to a distribution of forces which are parallel, rather than normal, to the area concerned. Such forces are associated with a shearing of the material, and are referred to as shear forces.

  • Where,
  • P is the total force
  • A the area over which it acts

06Hooke's law

Slide 16

Stress is directly proportional to strain within elastic limit of the material.

  • Where,
  • σ - Stress in ‘Pascal (or) N/m2’
  • ε - Strain (no unit)
  • E - Young Modulus (or) Proportional constant in ‘Pascal (or) N/m2’

07Stress–strain curve

Slide 17
  • The material will recover its shape if stretched to point 2.
  • There will be permanent deformation in the Material if the object is stretched to point 4.
  • Upto point 2 stress is proportional to strain.

08Elastic constants

Slide 18
  • Young Modulus (or) Modulus of elasticity - (E)
  • Shear Modulus (or) Modulus of Rigidity- (G)
  • Bulk Modulus - (K)
Slide 19
  • Young Modulus (or) Modulus of elasticity - (E)
  • The ratio of tensile or compressive stress to tensile or compressive strain.
Slide 20
  • Shear Modulus (or) Modulus of Rigidity- (G)
  • The ratio of shear stress to shear strain.
Slide 21
  • Bulk Modulus - (K)
  • The ratio of Direct or normal stress to Volumetric strain.

09Poisson's ratio

Slide 22

The ratio of Lateral strain to Linear strain (or) Longitudinal strain.

14Types of structures

Slide 47
  • There are two types of structures based on the number of unknowns.
  • Statically Determinate Sturctures
  • Statically Indeterminate Structures
Slide 48

The structures can be solved only with the help of static equilibrium equations (ΣV=0, ΣH=0, and ΣM=0), then the structures is named as Statically Determinate Structures.

Slide 49

EXAMPLES:

Slide 50

The structures can’t be solved only with the help of static equilibrium equations (ΣV=0, ΣH=0, and ΣM=0), then the structures is named as Statically Indeterminate Structures.

Here Compatability Equation will be used with static equilibrium equations to solve the structures.
